statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 11 sits in the low band and well below the block threshold, while Stress 52 in the elevated band reflects the crude and rate backdrop into the August month-end close.
recommendation: Conditional risk over the next 24 hours concentrates in the narrow 19:00-20:15 UTC window covering the US power hour and the August month-end market-on-close auction, and again around the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS cluster on 1 September. Outside those windows the evidence describes contained two-sided discovery.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds mid-range as the NQ overnight range stays untouched for an eighth hour, with Brent above $90 on the Hormuz strike and the 10-year yield above 4.75%
body:
Roughly three hours into the final August US cash session the Nasdaq-100 trades near 29,361.72, down 0.24% from a 29,433.43 previous close, inside an unchanged cash range of 29,304.49-29,465.00. The index sits about 57 points above its session low and about 103 points below its session high, so it is neither pinned at an extreme nor extending from one. NQ futures near 29,402.00 are off 0.30% and leave the 29,274.75-29,545.50 overnight range intact for an eighth consecutive hourly assessment, with neither extreme retested at any point today. That is the signature of contained two-sided price discovery rather than a persistent no-retracement trend.

The macro driver remains energy feeding into rates. Brent trades near $90.31, up 2.51%, and WTI near $85.64, up 2.68%, after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers that were preparing to lay mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Traders now price roughly a 62% chance of a September Federal Reserve rate increase, up from about 41% a week ago following Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole address. The Dallas Fed's August Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey, released at 14:30 UTC, added to that tone with a general business activity index of 11.6 against 1.3 in July, a production index of 16.1 and a raw-materials prices-paid index of 44.1.

Cross-asset confirmation is partial, which is the central reason Tail stays low. The 10-year Treasury yield is up about 4.4 basis points at 4.764%, its highest since January 2025, while the 2-year is unchanged at 4.35%. That is a bear steepening in which the policy-sensitive front end stays anchored despite the hawkish repricing, and it is the front end that would have to move to create the kind of violent directional repricing Tail measures. VIX is up 5.13% at 15.17 inside a 14.89-15.48 range and is trading below its own session high, a low absolute level for a session that opened after a military strike. Index leadership is split rather than aligned: the shared Finviz cross-asset file collected at 15:32 UTC shows six of eight megacaps lower with a mean change of -0.37% and a 2.0-point dispersion, against six of seven semiconductors higher with a mean of +0.61%, while sector breadth is negative with communication services off 1.62%. Nvidia is firm on its $3.5 billion convertible-bond investment in MediaTek tied to NVLink Fusion. Finviz futures show NQ off 0.19% against ES off 0.45% and YM off 0.65%, consistent with the live readings and used only as delayed supporting context.

Aggregating these, the pathological price path that Tail measures is not present. A genuine geopolitical discontinuity and a real inflation channel are live, but the index is mid-range, the futures range is stale for an eighth hour, retracement is working, the front end of the curve is calm, implied volatility is off its high and index leadership is split. Tail is set at 11 in the low band, one point below the previous hour, reflecting the additional hour of range containment. Stress at 52 in the elevated band reflects the unresolved oil and rate backdrop, negative breadth and month-end flow. Confidence at 88 reflects live index, futures, volatility, 2-year and 10-year yield and crude readings, a verified seven-day calendar, verified current reporting and a healthy 54-minute-old shared cross-asset file. The narrow 19:00-20:15 UTC window covering the power hour and the August month-end market-on-close auction is where conditional risk concentrates. Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The assessment applies jointly to NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments were available and every one mapped to EA_ON. Tail held at 5 through the Sunday US afternoon and the futures reopen, stepped to 9 at 22:00 UTC and to 14-15 across 23:00-00:00 UTC as the Iran escalation was first priced, then decayed back to 5 by 07:00-08:00 UTC. It spiked to the window peak of 17 at 09:00 UTC as crude extended, eased through 11, 10 and 9 over the following three hours, and firmed to 12-13 across 13:00-15:00 UTC around and after the US cash open. Stress climbed from 27 to a window peak of 53 at 14:00 UTC, with an intermediate dip to 47 at 12:00 UTC. Confidence ran between 82 and 88. Dominant mode was normal through the Sunday session, turned mixed once the escalation was priced, showed a single trend-down hour at 00:00 UTC, ran event/whipsaw at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC on the crude spike, and has been mixed for the last five hours. No hour in the window reached the watch band.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps the mapped state at EA_ON for all 24 hours, with conditional Tail never leaving the low band. It runs 11 in the current hour, holds 11-12 through the US early afternoon, then rises to 15 and a joint horizon peak of 16 for the 19:00 and 20:00 UTC power-hour and month-end cash-close pair, the only two slots carried as event/whipsaw on 31 August. It falls to 11 after the close and settles to an 8-9 overnight floor across the Asian session, where six hours are carried as normal. From the European pre-open it rebuilds gradually through 9-11, steps to 12-13 as US pre-market flow builds, reaches 14 at the 1 September cash open and returns to 16 for the 14:00 UTC hour carrying ISM Manufacturing, JOLTS and construction spending, easing to 14 in the post-release hour. Conditional Stress tracks the same shape between a 33 overnight floor and 56 at the two 31 August peaks, while Confidence decays from 88 to 62 across the horizon as observed evidence gives way to scheduled-catalyst inference.
